meta.subtitle: Samsara has turned GAAP-profitable with growth near 30%, but the current-year multiple already pays for a growth rate that is slowing.

analystCommentary: Coverage is bullish. Of 25 analysts, 19 rate Samsara Buy, 6 Hold and none Sell, for a consensus Buy. The consensus price target is $52.16, 34.1% above the September 24, 2026 price, with a median of $53.00 and a range of $39.00 to $60.00. The shares trade just below even the lowest target, so every analyst on the page sees some upside. The page carries no analyst rationale, so we cannot say which assumptions drive those targets. We land one notch below the consensus, at HOLD, for the valuation reasons argued in the valuation section, where our Bull case takes the Street's median target as its anchor.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Samsara Inc. sells the Connected Operations Platform, which ingests data from its IoT devices and from connected assets and third-party systems, with embedded capabilities for AI, workflows and analytics. Its applications include video-based safety, telematics and site visibility. Customers span transportation, construction, wholesale and retail trade, field services, logistics, manufacturing, utilities and energy, government, healthcare and education, and food and beverage. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its fiscal year ends on the Saturday closest to February 1, so fiscal 2026 ended on January 31, 2026, and the 10-Q covers the quarter ended August 1, 2026. Samsara reports as a single segment, and the page carries no product or geographic split. In each of its past two fiscal years, approximately 98% of revenue came from subscriptions to the platform; the rest came from replacement IoT devices, shipping and handling fees, and professional services. Subscription contracts typically have an initial term of three to five years and are generally non-cancelable and non-refundable, subject to limited exceptions, including for public-sector customers, who are often subject to annual budget appropriations cycles.

thesis.body: Samsara has crossed into GAAP profitability while revenue still grows near 30%, and free cash flow has turned positive; the financials section carries the figures. The question is the price. The shares trade at a current-year earnings multiple that already pays for growth the 10-K expects to keep slowing, and the trailing operating margin is barely above breakeven. Our Base values the shares a year out on FY2028 consensus earnings at a lower multiple than today's current-year multiple, which leaves a modest expected return against a bear case that is a real downside. The business is executing, but the valuation leaves little room for a slip, so we rate the shares HOLD.

catalysts: Sustained GAAP profitability: further profitable quarters would confirm the turn described in the financials section.
Recurring-revenue growth: annual recurring revenue and the count of customers above $100,000 in ARR are still rising (growth section).
Earnings delivery: consensus has EPS rising from FY2027 to FY2028, and delivering that path is what our Base case values.
Broader adoption: more Applications and Agents sold into existing accounts, and wider use beyond fleets, would deepen the platform, though the company says success in new use cases is uncertain.
Cash generation: free cash flow turned positive in FY2025 and rose in FY2026 (cash flow section).
risks: Valuation: the current-year multiple leaves little room for a slip in growth or margins (valuation section).
Slowing growth: annual revenue growth has slowed in each year shown, and the 10-K expects the rate to keep declining.
Thin operating profit: the trailing operating margin is barely positive, and most trailing net income comes from below the operating line.
Stock-based compensation: the 10-K says it will be a significant expense that affects profitability, and the page carries no figure to size it.
Founder voting control: insiders hold most of the vote through ten-vote Class B shares (management section).
Input costs: the MD&A names elevated hardware component, memory and storage costs and tariff policies among conditions that could affect results.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue for the quarter ended August 1, 2026 was $508.4 million, {+ up 29.9% +} from $391.5 million a year earlier. That quarter is the second quarter of Samsara's fiscal 2027; the page's snapshot labels it "Q3'26" on a calendar mapping, so we refer to it by its end date. Net income was {+ $16.2 million +}, against a net loss of $16.8 million a year earlier, and for the six months ended August 1, 2026 net income was $60.8 million against a $38.9 million loss. The 10-K says the company had incurred net losses in each period since incorporation before the third quarter of fiscal 2026, and fiscal 2026 as a whole still closed with a net loss of $9.1 million, so the turn is recent.

The profit is thinner at the operating line than the net line suggests. The trailing operating margin is 1.0%, the same as the latest quarter's, while the trailing net margin is 4.9%, so most trailing profit comes from below the operating line. The MD&A says that line consists primarily of income on money market funds and marketable debt securities and gains or losses on strategic investments.

Over the five fiscal years shown, operating margin improved from -82.6% in FY2022 to -3.2% in FY2026, and gross margin rose from 70.9% to 76.7%. The trailing gross margin of 76.4% sits slightly below the FY2026 level; the page gives no reason, and the MD&A says cost of revenue may increase with higher market prices for hardware components. Revenue growth has slowed each year, from 52.3% in FY2023 to 29.6% in FY2026, and consensus expects slower growth again in FY2027. The margin turn is real but early, and growth is decelerating.
financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet shows no strain, with one caveat about what the page captures. Cash and short-term investments were $0.3B at the end of FY2026, down from $0.9B in FY2022 after a low of $0.1B in FY2024, and total equity was $1.4B. The current ratio was 1.64 at fiscal year-end and is 1.62 on a trailing basis. The page shows a dash for total debt and net debt in every year, which means no figure was captured, so we do not describe the company as debt-free. The 10-K reports an accumulated deficit of $1,619.1 million as of January 31, 2026, the cumulative cost of the loss-making years. The MD&A adds that Samsara maintains a full valuation allowance against its U.S. deferred tax assets because it has concluded their realization is not more likely than not; we read that as a reminder that profitability is recent. Solvency is not the issue in this name; valuation and dilution are.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow turned before earnings did. FCF was $207.4M in FY2026, a 12.8% margin, after an 8.9% margin in FY2025 and negative margins from FY2022 through FY2024 (-44.6%, -20.9% and -2.4%). FY2026 capital expenditure was $28.8M, small against operating cash flow, so most operating cash reaches free cash flow. FY2026 free cash flow sat well above the full-year net loss noted in the income discussion, and the page does not break that gap down. Stock-based compensation is a non-cash expense that the 10-K says will be significant, so it is one item that can open such a gap, but no SBC figure is on the page to size it. The page shows no dividends and no buybacks in FY2025 or FY2026. Cash generation is real and rising, but at the trailing FCF yield discussed under valuation, cash flow alone does not support the price.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The trailing multiples carry little information. The P/E is 243.1x and EV/EBITDA is 722.2x because trailing earnings and EBITDA sit close to zero as the company crosses breakeven. Price-to-sales is 12.3x and the trailing FCF yield is 1.1%. The forward multiples matter more. The page shows a forward P/E of 50.5x, labelled NTM; on the page's own figures it matches the $38.90 price over the FY2027 consensus EPS of $0.77, so we treat it as the current-year multiple and use it as the like-for-like reference. On the FY2028 consensus EPS of $0.95, the shares trade at about 41.0x. One caution on basis: the FY2027 consensus EPS is far above the FY2026 diluted EPS of -$0.02 and a trailing operating margin barely above zero, and the page does not say whether the Street's estimates are on a GAAP basis, so the forward and trailing multiples may not compare. With no peer multiples on the page, we do not call the current-year multiple a premium or a discount to anything; the question is whether it holds as growth slows. The price sits between the 52-week low of $23.38 and the high of $47.47, and no source on the page explains the fall from the high.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Anchor: the Street's median target of $53.00. Growth holds near 30% as ARR and large-customer counts keep compounding, operating margin widens from near breakeven, and the market pays more for FY2028 earnings a year out than the 50.5x it pays for current-year earnings today. This is the case in which the Street's median view proves right.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Anchor: 45x the FY2028 consensus EPS of $0.95, a year out, a multiple we assume below today's current-year multiple because consensus has revenue growth slowing in FY2027 and the company expects further deceleration (risks section). Samsara delivers the consensus earnings path, and the multiple compresses as growth slows.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Anchor: 35x FY2028 EPS that comes in no higher than the FY2027 consensus of $0.77, a multiple we assume for a stock the market no longer prices for its current growth rate. Growth slows faster than consensus expects and operating margin stalls near breakeven. The result still sits above the 52-week low of $23.38.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The scenarios weight to a fair value of $41.36, an expected upside of 6.3% against a bear-case downside of 30.7%, for a reward/risk of 0.21×. That derives HOLD: expected upside is below the 10.0% BUY bar, and reward/risk is below 0.50×.

The Base carries 50% because the latest quarter and the ARR figures in the growth section are consistent with the consensus path. The Bull and Bear carry 25% each because the evidence on each side is of similar strength. For the Bull, no analyst rates the shares Sell and the price sits below every target; against it, the Bull needs a higher multiple a year out while growth slows. For the Bear, the company expects slower growth, the operating margin is barely positive, and the shares are well off the 52-week high noted above; against it, multi-year, generally non-cancelable subscriptions limit how fast revenue can fall, and free cash flow is positive.

Sensitivity runs both ways. Holding today's current-year multiple in the Base lifts expected upside above the BUY bar but leaves reward/risk below it, so the label stays HOLD; cutting the Base to today's FY2028 multiple puts it at about today's price, and the label still holds. Moving ten points of weight from Bear to Bull, or from Bull to Bear, also keeps HOLD. Combining the two changes does not: the current-year multiple with ten points moved toward the Bull derives BUY, and the FY2028 multiple with ten points moved toward the Bear derives SELL. HOLD sits between two defensible combinations, so it is a judgment rather than a finding.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Samsara reports as a single segment, and the page breaks out no product or geographic mix, so FY2026 revenue of $1.6B appears as one consolidated line. The 10-K says most revenue has historically come from subscriptions to Applications used with customers' fleets, and that the company has increased its focus on Applications for equipment, sites and frontline workers. Within the single line, growth comes from new customers and from selling more Applications and Agents to existing customers and expanding them across geographies and divisions, which the MD&A describes as expanding within the existing customer base. The business is one platform sold by subscription, and the shift beyond fleets is a stated direction that the page does not yet measure.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: Contracts typically run three to five years and are generally non-cancelable, and the MD&A says the platform and IoT devices are highly interdependent and form a combined performance obligation. Replacing a bundled hardware-and-software layer mid-contract should be costly for a customer. The page carries no retention or net-expansion figure, so we cannot measure how strong this is.

moatFactors.name: Multi-product adoption
moatFactors.body: The proxy filed June 1, 2026 reports that at the end of FY2026, 96% of customers with over $100,000 in ARR subscribed to 2+ products and 69% of those customers subscribed to 3+ products. Customers using several products are more embedded than single-product users, which supports the land-and-expand model among large accounts.

moatFactors.name: Data asset
moatFactors.body: The same proxy says Samsara processed more than 25 trillion data points in FY2026, which the company says enables its AI models to deliver deeper actionable insights. The page gives no evidence on whether rivals could build a comparable dataset, so we treat this as a possible advantage rather than an established one.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. The evidence for it is structural: multi-year, generally non-cancelable contracts, devices bundled with software into one performance obligation, and broad multi-product adoption among large customers. The evidence against it is mostly missing data: the page carries no retention, net-expansion or competitor figure, and the 10-K lists increased competition among the factors that could slow growth. The expansion beyond fleets, which the growth section notes the company itself calls uncertain, would test whether the same switching costs hold in new use cases. A wide rating would need retention evidence the page does not give; a rating of none would ignore contract terms and adoption figures that point to real switching costs.

points: Annual recurring revenue was $2,124,742 thousand as of August 1, 2026, against $1,640,113 thousand a year earlier. The company defines ARR as the annualized value of subscription contracts that have commenced revenue recognition, and says it is not a forecast.

Customers over $100,000 in ARR rose to 3,605 from 2,771 over the same year. The MD&A ties that growth to the company's focus on larger customers, its partner ecosystem and the release of more Applications.

The proxy filed June 1, 2026 reported $1.9 billion in ARR at the end of FY2026, up 30% year over year in constant currency, and 3,194 customers above that ARR threshold, up 29% year over year. The August figures show both measures still rising since then.
Revenue for the six months ended August 1, 2026 was $987.3 million, against $758.4 million a year earlier.
Consensus has FY2027 revenue at $2B, up 26%, and FY2028 revenue at $2.5B, so the Street models continued but slower growth.

New use cases: the 10-K says the company has increased its focus on Applications for equipment, sites and frontline workers, but that it is uncertain it will achieve the same penetration and organic growth there as with fleets.

management.leadership: According to the proxy statement filed June 1, 2026, Sanjit Biswas, a co-founder, is Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board. Co-founder John Bicket is Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, Dominic Phillips is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, and Adam Eltoukhy is Executive Vice President and Chief Administrative Officer and Corporate Secretary. Lara Caimi, formerly President of Worldwide Field Operations, stepped down effective March 3, 2025 and left the company on September 5, 2025. Both co-founders voluntarily received a minimal base salary of $50,000 each in FY2026, and the proxy says executive compensation is primarily delivered in the form of equity. The company is founder-led, and pay leans on equity rather than cash, which ties executives to the share price but adds to the stock-based compensation discussed under capital allocation.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is reinvestment. The cash flow section shows no dividends and no buybacks in the last two fiscal years, and the MD&A says the company expects research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the foreseeable future. The 10-K says future operating expenses will include a significant amount of stock-based compensation for RSUs already granted and any equity awards granted in the future, which will impact profitability levels. With positive free cash flow and cash and short-term investments on the balance sheet, the page shows no sign that the company needs outside capital. With no buyback on the page to offset it, equity compensation is the capital-allocation item that matters most for outside holders, and the page carries no figure to size it.
management.governance: The proxy filed June 1, 2026 says the Board has determined that eight of its ten directors are independent under NYSE rules: Mr. Andreessen, Mr. Bluedorn, Ms. Bostrom, Mr. Chadwick, Ms. Henry, Ms. Livermore, Mr. Steele and Ms. Wagner. Mr. Biswas holds both the Chief Executive Officer and Chair roles; the excerpt is truncated before any further description of board leadership. One related-party arrangement stands out: the company has a block charter agreement for an aircraft that Mr. Biswas beneficially owns through a limited liability company, operated by a third-party aviation company, and it paid $1,019,318 for business use in FY2026. The company says it pays an amount below market rates for comparable travel and that the agreement may be terminated on 30 days' prior written notice. A majority-independent board is a check, but with the combined Chief Executive Officer and Chair role and the voting structure set out under insider ownership, outside holders rely more on the founders' alignment than on board control.
management.insiderOwnership: As of April 15, 2026, the proxy counts 370,981,108 Class A shares, with one vote each, and 211,728,974 Class B shares, with ten votes each. Mr. Biswas beneficially owned 99,968,305 Class B shares, or 39.6% of total voting power, and Mr. Bicket 95,533,040 Class B shares, or 38.4%; neither holds a majority alone. The 12 directors and executive officers as a group held 90.3% of the Class B shares and 77.5% of total voting power. By contrast, Baillie Gifford & Co., an outside holder in the table, owned 15.5% of the Class A shares but 2.3% of the vote. If insiders vote together, outside Class A holders cannot carry a vote against them, and because each Class B share carries ten votes, insiders' voting power is well above their share of the equity.

idiosyncratic: Slowing growth against a high multiple: the 10-K says Samsara expects its revenue growth rate to continue to decline, including as a result of the maturation of its business. The valuation section shows that the expected return depends on the multiple compressing only modestly as that happens.

Thin operating profit: with the trailing operating margin barely positive and most trailing net income coming from below the operating line, heavier spending could return the company to operating losses. The MD&A expects each operating expense line to increase in absolute dollars, and the 10-K says the company may not achieve or sustain profitability in future periods.

Hardware and input costs: the MD&A says cost of revenue may increase as a result of higher market prices for hardware components, and cost of revenue includes the amortization of connected device costs, so higher device prices would weigh on margins of bundled subscriptions.
Dilution: the stock-based compensation discussed under capital allocation has no figure on the page, which leaves a gap in any valuation built on per-share earnings.
Founder control: the insider voting power set out under management limits outside holders' influence on all matters submitted to a stockholder vote.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says unfavorable economic conditions may negatively affect the growth of the business and its results. It lists inflationary pressure, foreign-currency fluctuations, interest-rate increases, supply-chain and freight disruptions, increased prices including elevated hardware component, memory, storage, computing and fuel costs, labor shortages, delayed or reduced spending on technology, and new trade and tariff policies. Samsara's customers operate in transportation, construction, logistics, manufacturing and other physical industries, and the 10-K lists macroeconomic factors among the reasons its growth rate could decline. Public-sector contracts carry the budget-appropriation exceptions noted in the overview, and the MD&A says foreign-currency exposure has increased as the company expanded globally. None of these is specific to Samsara, but a stock priced on the current-year multiple discussed under valuation has less room to absorb a macro-driven slowdown than one priced for slower growth.

body: We rate Samsara HOLD with a $36 to $44 target range. The business has turned GAAP-profitable, keeps adding recurring revenue and large customers, and generates free cash flow. But our scenarios weight to a fair value of $41.36, an expected upside of 6.3% against a bear-case downside of 30.7%, because the Base pays less for FY2028 earnings a year out than the market pays for current-year earnings today. That keeps us one notch below the Street's consensus Buy.

The target range is the band in which these scenarios derive HOLD. At or below the target low they derive BUY, and at or above the target high they derive SELL. Between those prices, the label moves only if new evidence moves the multiple or the weights, as the sensitivity in the valuation section shows.
